proof: `BOARD OF ASSESSORS`, PDF page 35 of the FY2015 annual town report. READ FROM THE TEXT LAYER, NOT RECOGNISED. The page prints FIVE separate tables and each is footed on its own; column names are read off the printed header (rule 13b.4), and the x band of every figure is given by its right edge, which is constant down each column. TABLE 1, `Fiscal 2015 Assessments and Revenues by Major Property Class`, five classes against the printed TOTALS row. Three columns foot exactly: the levy percentages to 100.0000, the valuations to 1,146,501,536 and the tax levy to 21,003,908.13. The levy is also the valuation at the printed rate -- 1,146,501,536 x 18.32/1000 = 21,003,908.14, a cent out because the rate is per thousand. THE INDUSTRIAL VALUATION IS PRINTED `20,155.100`, with a full stop where the thousands separator belongs; it is recorded here as 20,155,100, which is a PUNCTUATION defect and not a choice of digits -- every digit is present and in order. Two independent identities on this same page fix it: the column then foots to the printed 1,146,501,536 exactly, and the printed Industrial tax levy of 369,241.43 is 20,155,100 x 18.32/1000 to the cent (20,155.10 would give a levy of $369.24). The ABSTRACT table below reaches the same 1,146,501,536 by a different route. ALSO IN THIS FILE, as `line` rows because neither table prints a total: the `Valuation and Tax History`, nine fiscal years, where valuation x rate / 1000 reproduces the printed tax levy within a cent in ALL NINE years and each year's printed Change (%) reproduces the step in the levy; and `New Growth Revenue`, nine fiscal years, where the same arithmetic holds within $1 in SEVEN of the nine -- FY2009 prints 138,168 against 5,077,276 at 12.23 (=62,095) and FY2007 prints 295,074 against 23,809,803 at 12.41 (=295,480). Those two are NOT reconciled and no check here asserts them; the limit is registered as a gap. The FY2015 row of the history repeats the rate, the valuation, the account count and the levy printed in table 1 and the abstract, all four exactly.
